&nbsp;

::: {.alert .alert-info}

This article shows how to customize dynamic spectrograms, layer by layer. The [main vignette](dynaSpec.html) shows the basic usage of each layer. As there, the examples create interactive web pages: press play to watch the spectrogram along with the sound, click on it to play from that point, and use the speed slider to slow the sound down. Use `save_dynaspec()` with a file name ending in `.mp4` to create videos instead.

:::

```{r}
library(dynaSpec)
library(viridis)
library(seewave)

data("scythebill")
data("antshrike")
```

Some examples use recordings from the package [NatureSounds](https://cran.r-project.org/package=NatureSounds) or downloaded from the web (sounds must be 'Wave' objects or local '.wav' or '.mp3' files, so recordings are downloaded first).

Layers can be stored in an object and modified by adding more layers. Arguments of `ds_spectrogram()`, `ds_theme()` and style layers are combined with the previous ones (so only the settings that change need to be supplied), while other panel and player layers replace previous ones of the same kind, and annotations and captions are added. Settings not supplied take the defaults of each style. `dynaspec()` sets the frequency range shown (`flim`, in kHz) and the part of the sound used (`tlim`, in s: a single value takes the first seconds, two values a time interval).

# Spectrograms

`ds_spectrogram()` sets how the spectrogram is computed (window length `wl`, overlap `ovlp`, window function `wn`) and drawn (color palette `pal`, amplitude levels of the colors `collevels`, background `colbg`). Other arguments are passed to `seewave::spectro()`:

```{r}
ds_scythebill <- dynaspec(scythebill, flim = c(1.5, 5.5)) +
  ds_spectrogram(wl = 200, collevels = seq(-50, 0, 1))

# a longer recording for scrolling spectrograms
ds_antshrike <- dynaspec(antshrike, flim = c(0.5, 5.5)) +
  ds_spectrogram(wl = 256, collevels = seq(-50, 0, 1))

# palette and amplitude range
ds_scythebill + ds_spectrogram(pal = mako, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 1))
```

Black and white spectrogram with a wider amplitude range (fainter sounds are shown):

```{r}
ds_scythebill + ds_spectrogram(pal = reverse.gray.colors.1, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 5))
```

By default the background is the color of the lowest amplitude of the palette (dark purple for 'viridis'). A black background instead (when `colbg` is supplied, static spectrograms also use it as the background of the figure):

```{r}
ds_scythebill + ds_spectrogram(pal = viridis, colbg = "black")
```

In paged spectrograms the palette can also be the name of a 'viridis' palette (e.g. "magma") or two colors for a gradient, and `amp.trans` brightens the spectrogram (a nonlinear transformation that collapses the difference between loud and quiet sounds; 1 means no transformation):

```{r}
f <- list.files(
  system.file(package = "dynaSpec"),
  pattern = "\\.wav$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

swallow <- dynaspec(f[1]) +
  ds_spectrogram(amp.trans = 3, collevels = seq(-35, 0, 1)) +
  ds_paged() +
  ds_theme(axis.type = "standard")

swallow
```

# Panels

Oscillograms and amplitude envelopes can go above or below the spectrogram (`position`), with their own color (`col`) and height relative to the spectrogram (`height`). Power spectra go on the left or right side (`side`), with a given width (`width`, as a proportion of the figure):

```{r}
cols <- mako(10)

ds_scythebill +
  ds_spectrogram(pal = mako, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 1)) +
  ds_oscillogram(position = "above", col = cols[3], height = 0.3) +
  ds_spectrum(side = "left", col = cols[5], width = 0.12)
```

An amplitude envelope instead of the oscillogram (oscillograms and envelopes show the same information, so they are better not combined):

```{r}
ds_scythebill +
  ds_spectrogram(pal = mako, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 1)) +
  ds_envelope(col = cols[5], height = 0.3)
```

With several rows each row shows its own power spectrum, on the same scale:

```{r}
ds_scythebill +
  ds_spectrum(col = cols[5]) +
  ds_static(rows = 2, height = 350)
```

In scrolling spectrograms the lower panel can be an overview of the whole sound (`ds_overview()`, with its relative `height`), an oscillogram or an envelope:

```{r}
ds_antshrike +
  ds_envelope(col = cols[5]) +
  ds_scrolling(t.display = 2)
```

# Themes

`ds_theme()` sets the look of all styles: axis titles (`xlab`, `ylab`), the size of titles and labels (`cex.lab`, `cex.axis`), the font of titles (`font.lab`), the color of axes and text (`col.lab`) and of the axis labels alone (`col.axis`), the type of axes (`axis.type`) and the background around the panels (`bg`):

```{r}
ds_scythebill +
  ds_oscillogram() +
  ds_theme(
    xlab = "Time (s)",
    ylab = "Frequency (kHz)",
    cex.lab = 1.4,
    font.lab = 2,
    col.lab = "gray30"
  )
```

It also sets the font family of all text (`family`), the orientation of the axis labels of both axes (`las`, as in base R: 0 parallel to the axis, 1 horizontal, 2 perpendicular, 3 vertical), the length of ticks (`tick.length`), boxes around panels (`box`, `col.box`), grid lines (`grid`, `col.grid`), the background of oscillogram, envelope and spectrum panels (`col.panel`) and the color and size of titles (`col.title`, `cex.title`):

```{r}
ds_scythebill +
  ds_oscillogram() +
  ds_spectrum() +
  ds_theme(
    family = "serif",
    las = 1,
    tick.length = 0.3,
    box = FALSE,
    grid = TRUE,
    col.panel = "gray95"
  )
```

Themes can also set the colors of the plot: the spectrogram palette and background (`pal`, `colbg`), the color of oscillograms, envelopes and spectra (`col.wave`), the color of annotations (`col.annotation`), the play line (`col.line`) and the highlight box of paged spectrograms (`col.highlight`). These are used when they are not supplied in the other layers (e.g. `ds_spectrogram(pal = )` takes precedence). `col.bar` and `bg.bar` set the colors of the player controls of web pages. A dark theme:

```{r}
ds_scythebill +
  ds_oscillogram() +
  ds_theme(
    bg = "black",
    col.lab = "white",
    pal = viridis,
    colbg = "black",
    col.wave = viridis(10)[7],
    col.line = "white",
    col.bar = "white",
    bg.bar = "black"
  )
```

## Preset themes

Preset themes set several settings at once: `ds_theme_dark()`, `ds_theme_mako()` (light theme with the 'mako' palette for the spectrogram, panels, annotations and player controls), `ds_theme_presentation()` (large bold text for slides), `ds_theme_paper()` (black and white with serif fonts, for printed figures), `ds_theme_minimal()` (no boxes and light gray axes), `ds_theme_transparent()` (transparent background, to blend in slides or web pages of any color), `ds_theme_void()` (no axes or boxes), `ds_theme_xenocanto()` (inspired by the player of [Xeno-canto](https://xeno-canto.org)) and `ds_theme_macaulay()` (inspired by the player of the [Macaulay Library](https://www.macaulaylibrary.org)). Their settings can be changed in the call, or by adding `ds_theme()` afterwards (adding a preset replaces previous themes):

```{r}
ds_scythebill +
  ds_envelope() +
  ds_theme_dark(cex.lab = 1.3) +
  ds_player(buttons = c("time", "loop", "volume"))
```

```{r}
ds_scythebill +
  ds_oscillogram() +
  ds_theme_paper()
```

```{r}
ds_antshrike +
  ds_scrolling(t.display = 2) +
  ds_theme_presentation()
```

`ds_theme_xenocanto()` uses a gray spectrogram, labels inside the figure, a solid play line and rounded player controls with a seek bar. It looks best with scrolling spectrograms whose time axis moves along (`fix.time = FALSE`) and a short oscillogram:

```{r}
ds_antshrike +
  ds_oscillogram(height = 0.2) +
  ds_theme_xenocanto() +
  ds_scrolling(t.display = 3, fix.time = FALSE)
```

As other presets, its settings can be changed. For instance, the color version of the Xeno-canto player:

```{r}
ds_antshrike +
  ds_oscillogram(height = 0.2) +
  ds_theme_xenocanto(
    pal = viridis::inferno,
    colbg = "black",
    bg = "black",
    col.panel = "black",
    col.wave = "white",
    col.lab = "white",
    col.line = "white"
  ) +
  ds_scrolling(t.display = 3, fix.time = FALSE)
```

`ds_theme_macaulay()` uses a gray spectrogram, compact axes (frequency labels in a narrow column on the left and the time in minutes and seconds above the figure) and a black player bar with a square play button. It looks best with scrolling spectrograms with an overview of the whole sound below (the part shown is highlighted):

```{r}
ds_antshrike +
  ds_overview() +
  ds_theme_macaulay() +
  ds_scrolling(t.display = 3, fix.time = FALSE)
```

The look of these themes comes from settings that can be used in any theme. The Xeno-canto theme uses `axis.type = "inside"` (labels with units inside the figure), `lty.line` and `lwd.line` (type and width of the play line of scrolling spectrograms) and `bar.style = "rounded"` (round player controls with a seek bar, on the `bg.bar` background). The Macaulay theme uses `axis.type = "compact"`, `bar.style = "square"` (flat bar with a square play button in the color of the play line) and `col.highlight` (color dimming the overview outside the part shown).

`axis.type` can be "standard", "inside", "compact", "none" or, in scrolling spectrograms, "minimal" (1 s and 1 kHz scale bars):

```{r}
ds_antshrike +
  ds_scrolling(t.display = 2) +
  ds_theme(axis.type = "minimal")
```

## Theme of all spectrograms

`ds_set_theme()` sets a theme for all the spectrograms shown afterwards in the R session (e.g. in all the code chunks of a document), as `ggplot2::theme_set()`. `ds_theme()` added to a spectrogram changes some of its settings, and preset themes replace it. `ds_set_theme()` returns the previous theme, so it can be restored (`ds_set_theme(NULL)` removes it):

```{r}
old <- ds_set_theme(ds_theme_paper(cex.lab = 1.3))

# paper theme
ds_scythebill + ds_oscillogram()

# paper theme with another axis title
ds_scythebill + ds_envelope() + ds_theme(ylab = "Freq. (kHz)")

# restore the previous theme
ds_set_theme(old)
```

# Static spectrograms

Static spectrograms are the default style, so `ds_static()` is only needed to change their settings or to switch back from another style (the last style added is used). `ds_static()` sets the color of the play line and active buttons (`lcol`), the size and resolution of each row (`width`, `height`, in pixels, and `res`), the number of rows (`rows`), whether the play line is shown (`play.line`) and the frames per second of videos (`fps`):

```{r}
ds_scythebill +
  ds_static(lcol = "#E69F00", width = 1200, height = 400, res = 120)
```

Without the moving line (clicking on the figure still plays the sound from that point):

```{r}
ds_scythebill + ds_static(play.line = FALSE)
```

# Scrolling spectrograms

`ds_scrolling()` sets the time window shown (`t.display`), whether the time axis moves along with the spectrogram (`fix.time = FALSE`), the play line (`lcol`, `lty`, `lwd`), the initial speed (`speed`), a delay before the spectrogram starts moving (`buffer`, in s), looping (`loop`), the size and resolution of the frames (`width`, `height`, `res`) and the frames per second of videos (`fps`):

```{r}
ds_antshrike +
  ds_spectrogram(pal = viridis, colbg = "black") +
  ds_oscillogram(col = "#31688E99") +
  ds_scrolling(
    t.display = 2,
    fix.time = FALSE,
    speed = 0.5,
    lcol = "white",
    lty = 1,
    width = 1000,
    height = 500,
    res = 120
  )
```

Long-billed hermit song at 1/5 speed, without axes and looping (web pages loop until paused):

```{r}
data("Phae.long4", package = "NatureSounds")

dynaspec(Phae.long4, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  ds_spectrogram(
    wl = 300,
    ovlp = 90,
    pal = magma,
    collevels = seq(-50, 0, 5),
    colbg = "black"
  ) +
  ds_scrolling(
    t.display = 1.7,
    width = 1000,
    height = 500,
    res = 120,
    speed = 0.2,
    loop = 3
  ) +
  ds_theme(axis.type = "none")
```

The first 20 s of a northern nightingale wren recording from [xeno-canto](https://www.xeno-canto.org) using a custom color palette:

```{r}
nightingale_wren <- tempfile(fileext = ".mp3")
download.file(
  "https://xeno-canto.org/518334/download",
  nightingale_wren,
  mode = "wb"
)

custom_pal <- colorRampPalette(c(
  "#2d2d86",
  "#2d2d86",
  reverse.terrain.colors(10)[5:10]
))

dynaspec(nightingale_wren, flim = c(0, 8), tlim = 20) +
  ds_spectrogram(
    wl = 600,
    ovlp = 95,
    pal = custom_pal,
    collevels = seq(-40, 0, 5),
    colbg = "#2d2d86"
  ) +
  ds_scrolling(
    t.display = 3,
    width = 700,
    height = 250,
    res = 100,
    lcol = "#FFFFFFE6"
  )
```

Spix's disc-winged bat inquiry call slowed down 16 times (`speed = 0.0625`, the slowest speed web browsers can play):

```{r}
data("thyroptera.est", package = "NatureSounds")

# extract one call
thy_wav <- attributes(thyroptera.est)$wave.objects[[12]]

# convert to 16 bits (as the silence added below)
thy_wav <- tuneR::normalize(thy_wav, unit = "16")

# add silence at both sides
thy_wav <- pastew(
  tuneR::silence(
    duration = 0.05,
    samp.rate = thy_wav@samp.rate,
    xunit = "time"
  ),
  thy_wav,
  output = "Wave"
)
thy_wav <- pastew(
  thy_wav,
  tuneR::silence(
    duration = 0.04,
    samp.rate = thy_wav@samp.rate,
    xunit = "time"
  ),
  output = "Wave"
)

dynaspec(thy_wav, flim = c(12, 45)) +
  ds_spectrogram(
    wl = 400,
    ovlp = 95,
    pal = inferno,
    collevels = seq(-40, 0, 5),
    colbg = "black"
  ) +
  ds_oscillogram(col = inferno(10, alpha = 0.9)[3]) +
  ds_scrolling(
    t.display = 0.08,
    width = 700,
    height = 250,
    res = 100,
    lcol = "#FFFFFFE6",
    lty = 1,
    speed = 0.0625,
    loop = 4
  )
```

Other options of `ds_scrolling()` are a custom spectrogram function (`spectro.call`, a call made with `base::call()`), spectral derivatives (`derivative = TRUE`, requires the package 'imager') and the window length in ms (`hop.size`).

# Paged spectrograms

`ds_paged()` sets the duration of each page (`t.display`), the highlight box (`highlight.col`, `highlight.alpha`), the cursor (`lcol`), a title (`title`), an amplitude color scale (`plot.legend = TRUE`), the size of the pages (`spec.width`, `spec.height`, in inches) and the frames per second of videos (`fps`). Other arguments set the preparation of the pages (e.g. `resample.rate`, `amp.thresh` or `filter`):

```{r}
swallow +
  ds_paged(
    title = "Female barn swallow",
    highlight.col = "#2d2d86",
    highlight.alpha = 0.4,
    lcol = "#FFEA46"
  ) +
  ds_theme(bg = "black")
```

The first 12 s of a humpback whale song, with 3 s pages and the frequency range used by these whales (0-700 Hz):

```{r}
whale <- tempfile(fileext = ".wav")
download.file(
  "http://www.oceanmammalinst.org/songs/hmpback3.wav",
  whale,
  mode = "wb"
)

dynaspec(whale, flim = c(0, 0.7), tlim = 12) +
  ds_spectrogram(amp.trans = 3) +
  ds_paged(t.display = 3)
```

A common nighthawk call from [xeno-canto](https://www.xeno-canto.org) with a two-color palette:

```{r}
nighthawk <- tempfile(fileext = ".mp3")
download.file("https://xeno-canto.org/490771/download", nighthawk, mode = "wb")

dynaspec(nighthawk, tlim = 20) +
  ds_spectrogram(pal = c("white", "black")) +
  ds_paged(t.display = 4, highlight.col = "#d1b0ff", lcol = "#7817ff")
```

# Annotations

`ds_annotations()` highlights parts of the sound with translucent boxes. It takes a data frame with the start and end of each selection (in s), as the selection tables of [warbleR](https://cran.r-project.org/package=warbleR) and [ohun](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ohun). If it has 'bottom.freq' and 'top.freq' columns (in kHz) the boxes only span that frequency range, and colors and labels can be taken from its columns:

```{r}
# note types
st <- data.frame(
  start = c(0.34, 1.13, 1.44, 1.75),
  end = c(1.03, 1.36, 1.68, 2.28),
  bottom.freq = c(2.5, 2.4, 2.3, 2.1),
  top.freq = c(3.9, 4, 3.8, 5.4),
  labels = c("A", "B", "B", "C"),
  colors = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#56B4E9", "#009E73")
)

ds_scythebill + ds_annotations(st, col = "colors", labels = "labels")
```

The box borders are set with `border` (a color or the name of a column with the color of each box), `lwd` (width) and `lty` (line type):

```{r}
ds_scythebill +
  ds_annotations(
    st,
    col = "colors",
    alpha = 0.1,
    border = "colors",
    lwd = 2,
    lty = "dashed",
    labels = "labels"
  )
```

`ds_annotations()` also sets the opacity of the boxes (`alpha`), the size of the labels (`cex`) and whether boxes span only the frequency range of the selections (`freq`). The following code highlights the male and female parts of a house wren duet (after downloading the recording and selection table from GitHub):

```{r}
# house wren male-female duet recording
hs_wren <- tempfile(fileext = ".wav")
download.file(
  "https://github.com/maRce10/example_sounds/raw/refs/heads/main/house_wren_male_female_duet.wav",
  hs_wren,
  mode = "wb"
)

# and selection table
st <- read.csv(
  "https://github.com/maRce10/example_sounds/raw/refs/heads/main/house_wren_male_female_duet.csv"
)

# colors and labels
st$colors <- viridis(10)[c(3, 8)]
st$labels <- c("male", "female")

duet <- dynaspec(hs_wren, flim = c(1, 13)) +
  ds_spectrogram(
    wl = 512,
    pal = reverse.gray.colors.1,
    collevels = seq(-100, 0, 1)
  ) +
  ds_scrolling(t.display = 1.2, loop = 3, width = 1000, height = 500, res = 120)

duet + ds_annotations(st, col = "colors", alpha = 0.4, labels = "labels", cex = 1.5)
```

With box borders, spanning the whole frequency range (`freq = FALSE`), and an oscillogram:

```{r}
duet +
  ds_annotations(
    st,
    col = "colors",
    alpha = 0.3,
    border = "gray30",
    lwd = 2,
    freq = FALSE
  ) +
  ds_oscillogram()
```

`type = "spectrogram"` colors the spectrogram itself within each selection, with a gradient from the spectrogram background to the color of the selection (as `warbleR::color_spectro()`), instead of drawing boxes. A narrower amplitude range (`collevels`) keeps the background noise uncolored:

```{r}
duet +
  ds_spectrogram(collevels = seq(-60, 0, 1)) +
  ds_annotations(st, col = "colors", type = "spectrogram", labels = "labels")
```

Selection tables made with [warbleR](https://cran.r-project.org/package=warbleR) can be used directly. When they have selections of several sound files, only those of the sound shown are used (matching the file name), or the sound file is chosen with `sound.file` (e.g. for 'Wave' objects):

```{r}
data("lbh_selec_table", package = "warbleR")
data("Phae.long1", package = "NatureSounds")

dynaspec(Phae.long1, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  ds_spectrogram(wl = 300) +
  ds_annotations(lbh_selec_table, sound.file = "Phae.long1.wav", labels = "selec")
```

# Captions

`ds_captions()` adds text at a fixed position of the figure (`x` and `y`, as proportions of the figure width and height), shown during a time range of the sound (`start` and `end`, in s). `fading` adds fade-in and fade-out effects (in s), and `col`, `cex` and `font` set the color, size and font. Several captions can be shown one after the other, and several caption layers can be added at different positions. The following code labels the frog species calling in a recording from Costa Rica:

```{r}
# frog recording from GitHub
frogs <- tempfile(fileext = ".wav")
download.file(
  "https://github.com/maRce10/example_sounds/raw/refs/heads/main/CostaRican_frogs.wav",
  frogs,
  mode = "wb"
)

dynaspec(frogs, flim = c(0, 5.5), tlim = c(35.3, 50.5)) +
  ds_spectrogram(
    wl = 512,
    ovlp = 95,
    pal = cividis,
    collevels = seq(-60, 0, 5),
    colbg = "black"
  ) +
  ds_oscillogram(col = "#31688E", height = 1 / 3) +
  ds_captions(
    c("Dendropsophus ebraccatus", "Eleutherodactylus coqui"),
    start = c(35.7, 42.3),
    end = c(40.8, 50.1),
    x = 0.3,
    y = 0.9,
    col = "#FFEA46CC",
    font = 3,
    fading = 0.6
  ) +
  ds_scrolling(
    t.display = 1.1,
    loop = 3,
    width = 1200,
    height = 550,
    res = 200,
    lcol = "#FFFFFFCC",
    lty = 3
  ) +
  ds_theme(bg = "black", col.lab = "white")
```

Note that times of annotations and captions refer to the original recording, even when only part of it is used (`tlim`).

# Player

`ds_player()` sets the speeds offered by the speed slider of web pages (the first one is the initial speed; a single speed hides the slider), whether the pitch is kept when slowing down by default and the additional controls shown (`buttons`). A player with only the play button, for instance to embed in a presentation:

```{r}
ds_scythebill + ds_player(speeds = 1, buttons = character())
```

A player with all controls, starting at half speed and looping (the loop button starts pressed when `ds_scrolling(loop)` is larger than 1):

```{r}
ds_antshrike +
  ds_player(
    speeds = c(0.5, 1, 0.25),
    buttons = c("time", "loop", "volume", "download", "fullscreen")
  ) +
  ds_scrolling(t.display = 2, loop = 2)
```

In scrolling spectrograms, `buttons = "zoom"` adds a slider (with - and + buttons) to stretch or shrink the spectrogram, from 4 times less to 4 times more time than `t.display` (at most the whole sound). The spectrogram is drawn at twice the resolution so zooming in stays sharp, which makes web pages larger:

```{r}
ds_antshrike +
  ds_overview() +
  ds_theme_macaulay() +
  ds_player(buttons = c("zoom", "volume", "time")) +
  ds_scrolling(t.display = 3, fix.time = FALSE)
```

The download button saves the sound embedded in the web page (named after the sound file or 'Wave' object), and the full screen button enlarges the player to the size of the screen (e.g. for presentations; web browsers may not allow full screen in embedded frames).

# Videos

Videos (`save_dynaspec()` with a file name ending in `.mp4`) use the same settings as web pages. Videos of scrolling spectrograms render every frame, which can be sped up by using several cores (`parallel`) and lowering the frames per second (`fps`):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
save_dynaspec(duet + ds_scrolling(parallel = 4, fps = 30), "house_wren_duet.mp4")
```
